title: Magnetic Chess Board
description: A Pico W chessboard with magnetic sensors that records physical moves and sends game states to a local web interface.

cover.alt: Rendering of the magnetic chess board and its pieces

details: The board uses a matrix of reed switches beneath the squares to sense where pieces are present. A Raspberry Pi Pico W scans that physical state and sends it over Wi-Fi to a local Flask server.

The server compares the new position with the saved game state using python-chess, finds the matching legal move, and updates the move history. When more than one move could fit, the OLED and two buttons let the player choose.
Each game is saved for later review, including a local web view. I designed the board, pieces, and PCB around the challenge of turning a normal physical game into a record you can inspect afterward.
